findings.statement: The state plan must provide for review of drug therapy before each prescription is filled or delivered to a beneficiary, with applicable state law establishing standards for counseling of the beneficiary or caregiver; the state must give pharmacies detailed compliance information, which pharmacies must pass on to their pharmacists [42-CFR-456.705(a)].

The state plan must provide for point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review of drug therapy using predetermined standards before each prescription is filled or delivered, and that review must include screening to identify potential drug therapy problems of specified types [42-CFR-456.705(b)].

The screening must identify: (1) therapeutic duplication (two or more drugs from the same class where the combined daily dose risks an adverse result or extra program cost without added benefit); (2) drug-disease contraindication; (3) adverse drug-drug interaction; (4) incorrect drug dosage (strength x quantity dispensed / days supply falling outside standards); (5) incorrect duration of drug treatment; (6) drug-allergy interactions; and (7) clinical abuse/misuse [42-CFR-456.705(b), 42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].

Prospective drug review and retrospective DUR (including interventions and education) are not required for drugs dispensed to residents of nursing facilities that comply with the drug regimen review procedures in 42 CFR part 483, though a state may elect to make such drugs subject to all DUR requirements [42-CFR-456.703(b)].

Counseling standards are part of prospective drug review: state law or another method satisfactory to the state agency must set standards for pharmacist counseling, including special situations such as offsite or mail delivery, whether offers apply to new vs. refill prescriptions, and who may make the offer [42-CFR-456.705(c)].

The same seven screening categories (by cross-reference to 456.705(b)(1)-(7)) plus therapeutic appropriateness, over/underutilization, and generic product use are also monitored retrospectively using predetermined standards [42-CFR-456.709(b)].

Predetermined standards used in DUR must derive from peer-reviewed literature and specified compendia (AHFS Drug Information, USP-DI, AMA Drug Evaluations), with differences resolved by physician-pharmacist consensus, and must be available to the public with pharmacists and physicians informed of them [42-CFR-456.703(f), 42-CFR-456.703(g)].

The screening must identify: (1) therapeutic duplication (two or more drugs from the same class where the combined daily dose risks an adverse result or extra program cost without added benefit); (2) drug-disease contraindication; (3) adverse drug-drug interaction; (4) incorrect drug dosage (strength x quantity dispensed / days supply falling outside standards); (5) incorrect duration of drug treatment; (6) drug-allergy interactions; and (7) clinical abuse/misuse [42-CFR-456.705(b), 42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].

Prospective drug review and retrospective DUR (including interventions and education) are not required for drugs dispensed to residents of nursing facilities that comply with the drug regimen review procedures in 42 CFR part 483, though a state may elect to make such drugs subject to all DUR requirements [42-CFR-456.703(b)].

Counseling standards are part of prospective drug review: state law or another method satisfactory to the state agency must set standards for pharmacist counseling, including special situations such as offsite or mail delivery, whether offers apply to new vs. refill prescriptions, and who may make the offer [42-CFR-456.705(c)].

The same seven screening categories (by cross-reference to 456.705(b)(1)-(7)) plus therapeutic appropriateness, over/underutilization, and generic product use are also monitored retrospectively using predetermined standards [42-CFR-456.709(b)].

Predetermined standards used in DUR must derive from peer-reviewed literature and specified compendia (AHFS Drug Information, USP-DI, AMA Drug Evaluations), with differences resolved by physician-pharmacist consensus, and must be available to the public with pharmacists and physicians informed of them [42-CFR-456.703(f), 42-CFR-456.703(g)].
